title: Choosing a career path
examples: What is the difference between a degree and an apprenticeship?
How can I figure out what I am actually interested in?
Do I need to know exactly what job I want right now?

explain.say: First we will talk about understanding your interests.
Next we will look at different career routes available to you.
Then we will learn about apprenticeships as a strong option.
An everyday example is choosing a trade like plumbing.
A common mistake is thinking you must choose one thing forever.

items: You can change your mind later.

faq.q: Do I have to know my exact career right now?
faq.a: No, you do not need to know your exact career right now. Think of it as exploring options.
asks: When should I decide my job?
Is it okay to change my mind later?

faq.q: What is the main difference between a degree and an apprenticeship?
faq.a: A degree focuses more on academic study, while an apprenticeship combines paid work with learning. Both are valuable.
asks: Which one is better for me?

faq.q: How do I figure out what my interests really are?
faq.a: Try listing things you enjoy doing in your free time. Your hobbies can point you toward career fields.
asks: Where do I find my passion?

faq.q: Are apprenticeships only for manual jobs?
faq.a: No, apprenticeships exist in many fields, including technology and healthcare. They teach skilled roles.
asks: Can I do an apprenticeship in an office job?
What kind of jobs use apprenticeships?

faq.q: What should I do after I finish school?
faq.a: You have choices like university, college courses, or starting an apprenticeship. It depends on your goals.
asks: What is the next step after Year 11?

facts: Interests are the things you naturally enjoy doing.
A university degree focuses heavily on academic theory.
An apprenticeship combines paid work experience with formal learning.
It is normal to change your career path as you grow.

quiz.say: If you love solving problems with machines, which path might be a good starting point?

options.show: D. Just waiting until I am older
options.say: D. Just waiting until I am older

quiz.why: An apprenticeship allows you to practice skills in a real working environment.

wrong.0: This focuses on reading and theory, not building or fixing things.
wrong.1: This is usually more focused on creative skills than technical building.
wrong.2: Waiting means missing out on practical learning opportunities now.

quiz.say: Which option best combines earning money while learning a trade?
quiz.why: The core of an apprenticeship is working and getting paid while you learn.

wrong.0: University usually requires you to pay fees and focus only on study.
wrong.1: Reading alone does not give you the practical experience needed for a job.
wrong.2: While helpful, volunteering does not usually provide a formal salary or structured training.

quiz.say: If your main interest is helping people feel better, what is a good general area to explore?
quiz.why: These fields directly use skills related to helping and caring for others.

wrong.0: Farming is more focused on agriculture and the land.
wrong.2: Finance usually involves numbers, money, and business records.
wrong.3: Programming focuses more on logic and writing code.
